# Atom configuration fields

The frontmatter of an `.atom.astro` file exports one literal object:

```astro
---
import type { Props, Input, Output } from '../.atomic/types/<atom-name>';
import type { AtomConfig } from '../.atomic/types/authoring';
const { input }: Props = Astro.props;
export const config: AtomConfig<Input, Output> = {
  description: '…',
};
---
```

The import paths are relative from the atom file to `.atomic/types/` in the project root; `atomic check` writes those declarations. Values are literals: no variables, calls or spreads. Only `validate` holds functions.

## Project layout

A project is the directory holding `atomic.yaml` (a repository of agents) or `.atomic/atomic.yaml` (atomic embedded in another repository). The smallest manifest is:

```yaml
atomic: 1
name: <project-name>
```

Paths are relative to the manifest's directory. atomic finds files by these default globs:

- atoms: `atoms/**/*.atom.astro`, `**/*.atom.astro`
- workflows: `workflows/**/*.workflow.yaml`, `**/*.workflow.yaml`
- schemas: `schemas/**/*.schema.yaml`, `schemas/**/*.schema.json`
- evals: `evals/**/*.yaml`, `evals/**/*.jsonl`
- toolsets: `toolsets/**/*.openapi.yaml`, `toolsets/**/*.openapi.json`

An atom's schemas default to sidecars named after its file: for `atoms/<stem>.atom.astro`, `atoms/<stem>.input.schema.yaml` and `atoms/<stem>.output.schema.yaml` (`.json` also works; both forms of one sidecar is an error). Eval cases for atom `<name>` go in `evals/<name>/`, one case per `.yaml` file or one per line of a `.jsonl` file. `.atomic/types/` is generated: never edit it, and keep it out of version control.

## Fields

Every field is optional.

- **`atomic`** (`1`): The atom format version. Omit it. The only version is `1`.
- **`description`** (`string`): One sentence saying what the atom does. Defaults to the name; always write one.
- **`name`** (`string`): The atom's identity. Defaults to the file name without `.atom.astro`. Set it only to keep an identity across a rename.
- **`version`** (`number`): A positive integer, default 1. Raise it when the input or output contract changes.
- **`kind`** (`'lite' | 'codex' | 'exec' | 'a2a'`): How the atom runs. `lite` (the default) is one model call with structured output and no tools. `codex` is a Codex agent thread that may read, and with `sandbox: 'workspace-write'` change, a repository. `exec` runs a command with no model. This version runs `codex`, `lite`, `exec`. The type also allows `a2a`, which `atomic check` refuses. `a2a` is staged: the catalog checks it, and the production loader refuses it until remote atoms ship.
- **`input`** (`unknown`): The full JSON Schema 2020-12 of the input, inline or as `{$ref: './file.schema.yaml'}`. Omit it to use the sidecar file described under Project layout.
- **`output`** (`unknown`): The full JSON Schema of the output, inline, by `$ref` or as a sidecar. For `lite` and `codex` atoms it must lower to the generation profile in strict-schemas.md.
- **`model`** (`string`): A model name or a tier the project maps to a model. Omit it to take the project default. Tiers: `basic`, `fast`, `advanced`, `frontier`.
- **`sandbox`** (`'read-only' | 'workspace-write'`): `read-only` (the default) or `workspace-write`. Only `codex` atoms touch files.
- **`network`** (`false | {allow: string[]}`): Omit it or write `false`: this version runs atoms with no network, and refuses an allow list.
- **`tools`** (`unknown`): Omit it: this version refuses atoms that declare tools.
- **`trust`** (`'external' | 'team' | 'agent'`): Who the input comes from: `team`, `agent` or `external`. Omit it for team-curated input.
- **`approvals`** (`unknown`): In-turn approval policy for `codex` atoms. Omit it; atoms never ask.
- **`budget`** (`unknown`): Spending limits for one run. Omit it to inherit the finite project defaults.
- **`retry`** (`unknown`): Repair and retry policy. Omit it to use the defaults.
- **`validate`** (`((context: Context<I, O, C, R>) => boolean)[]`): A list of expression-bodied arrow functions over `{input, output}` that return a boolean, for rules a schema cannot state. A `false` result rejects the answer and the rule's source goes back to the model for repair. Never quoted CEL strings.
- **`evals`** (`unknown`): The directory of eval cases, relative to the atom file. Omit it to use `evals/<name>/` beside the manifest.
- **`exec`** (`unknown`): For `kind: 'exec'`: `{command: ['program', 'arg', …]}`. The command reads the input as JSON on standard input and writes the output as JSON on standard output.
- **`effects`** (`unknown`): Outside-world effects an `exec` atom performs. Omit it for atoms that only compute.
- **`env`** (`unknown`): Public environment variable names the atom may read through its context. Never secrets.
- **`scorers`** (`Record<string, Scorer<I, O, C, J, R>>`): Bindings from a declared judge to a numeric score with a `min_mean` threshold between 0 and 1. Leave out unless the task needs a judge.
- **`examples`** (`{name: string; input: I; output: O}[]`): Named `{name, input, output}` examples. `atomic check` validates both values against the full schemas. Write at least one.
- **`context`** (`unknown`): The schema of public execution context the prompt reads, or a `<file-stem>.context.schema.yaml` sidecar. Leave out unless the prompt reads context.
- **`case`** (`unknown`): The schema of the metadata eval cases carry for judges. Leave out unless the atom has judges.
- **`judges`** (`unknown`): Judge input and output schemas by judge name, used by `scorers`. Leave out unless the task needs a judge.

In the types, `I`, `O`, `C` and `R` are the generated `Input`, `Output`, case and context types.

## Refused by this version

`atomic check` fails on these fields, saying they are not supported yet: `extends`, `review`, `credentials`, `runtime`, `codex`, `skills`, `remote`, `auth`. Any other field name fails as unknown.
